title: Implications of Alpha and Beta Human Papillomaviruses Infection in the Oral Microbiome from Mexican Subjects Living with HIV
content: Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection and oral microbiota alterations have been independently associated with oral disease in people living with HIV (PLHIV). However, the relationship between alpha-HPV (α-HPV), beta-HPV (β-HPV), and the oral microbiome remains poorly understood. Aim: This cross-sectional study aimed to describe the association between oral HPV infection and the oral and oropharyngeal microbiome in Mexican PLHIV with sustained virologic control and immune reconstitution. Methods: Oral and oropharyngeal samples were obtained by rinsing and gargling, and participants were classified into HPV-negative, α-HPV, and β-HPV groups. The V3–V4 region of the 16S rRNA gene was sequenced using the Illumina MiSeq platform. A total of 65 participants were included in the final analysis: 19 HPV-negative, 16 -α-HPVpositive, and β-HPV 30 -positive. Results: Alpha diversity was significantly increased in both HPV-positive groups compared with the HPV-negative group, with the highest diversity observed in the α-HPV positive group. The α-HPV group also showed a higher Fusobacteriota/Bacteroidota ratio and enrichment of Fusobacteriota-related taxa. In addition, predicted functional analysis showed enrichment of pathways related to lysine and pyruvate fermentation to butyrate in the α-HPV group. These findings suggest that α- and β-HPV infections may be associated with different oral microbial ecosystems in PLHIV.
